market_mistake: BOUNDARY DECLARED 2026-09-02 — ORCL IS INSIDE the scaled-cloud set. The prior draft placed the boundary at MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL by name and flagged ORCL as sitting on it; the operator has ruled it inside. BASIS (OPERATOR-SUPPLIED, not machine-read from filings — this repo's own scan read of ORCL is `quantified-revenue-share`, and the figures below were not verified by it): Oracle is no longer valued as a legacy software company but priced explicitly as an AI compute platform — $638bn RPO (+363% YoY), OCI +93% to $5.8bn — and the live debate about it is backlog CONVERSION. CONSEQUENCE, TAKEN RATHER THAN SOFTENED: THE CLASS CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN. 'The market misprices who captures the layer' cannot stand as a statement about scaled clouds, because the scaled cloud the market ALREADY credits as a compute winner is also the one quantifying its revenue share. Inside the boundary the claim is not weakened, it is inverted, so it is redrawn rather than edited. WHAT THE CARD NOW CLAIMS, narrowed to three names: MSFT, AMZN and GOOGL neither quantify their AI-compute economics nor are priced primarily as compute platforms, and among THOSE THREE the market's attribution of the layer's economics is untested. The scarce assets — compute SOLD, interconnection OWNED — are held in part by operators the market prices as financing vehicles rather than as parties capturing economics. THE ASYMMETRY IS NOT THE EVIDENCE AND ITS CAUSE IS NOT STRUCTURAL. ORCL and BABA both reach quantified-revenue-share while running cloud at scale, so aggregation is a CHOICE. That retraction does not license the reverse inference: choice-not-structure still does not permit reading attribution off the FORM of disclosure — the same absent-evidence error with a new justification. Disclosure here measures INCENTIVE and never economics: neoclouds publish binding contracts because the contract is the collateral they finance against; crypto-origin operators publish them as proof the pivot is real; ORCL and BABA quantify where quantifying helps them; incumbents aggregate for competitive reasons. CONSEQUENCE: the big three's AI-compute economics are NOT MEASURABLE from their filings in either direction, which is why this card rests on CONVERSION and never on who publishes a contract.
null_thesis: The parties the market already favours are the parties that capture it: the neocloud contracted backlog proves to be a financing artifact that does not convert to recognized revenue at the contracted duration, and owners of land, substation and grid interconnect are repriced as landlords rather than as holders of the scarce asset. The attribution claim is wrong and the market's existing attribution is right.

first_confirming.trigger: At the next quarterly print of CRWV — the one name in the cohort that reports both sides — REVENUE RECOGNIZED AGAINST PRIOR-PERIOD REMAINING PERFORMANCE OBLIGATIONS rises, or the RPO-to-revenue duration SHORTENS. Accumulation is not the test: a backlog that never converts still grows, so 'contracted backlog grows' is consistent with this thesis and its null simultaneously. CONVERSION is where the two diverge.
first_confirming.basis: one full scheduled print cycle; CRWV already discloses both RPO and recognized revenue ($60.7bn RPO at 2025-12-31 against $15.1bn a year earlier), so both sides of the ratio are published line items. Deliberately ONE NAME and ONE RATIO: an OR across five names is near-certain to trigger on something, which is a test that cannot fail. NOTED, NOT ADDED: after the 2026-09-02 boundary ruling, ORCL's own market debate is this same backlog-conversion ratio at far larger scale — which says conversion is the LAYER's discriminator rather than a CRWV idiosyncrasy, and is the strongest external support for this choice of test. ORCL is deliberately NOT added as a second trigger: two names joined by OR restores exactly the cannot-fail shape this trigger was re-cut to remove. It is an independent read to consult when CRWV prints, not part of the test.

falsifiers.trigger: Recognized revenue against prior-period RPO FALLS, or RPO-to-revenue duration LENGTHENS, across two consecutive prints — the backlog is accumulating without converting, which is the null's own signature.
falsifiers.basis: two-plus scheduled print cycles of a disclosed ratio. PROPOSED — operator to select.

falsifiers.trigger: Counterparty concentration breaks the cohort: a named counterparty behind the binding contracts insources or cancels, and the contracted backlog is revealed as one customer rather than a market. BLZE's case already rests on a single contracted counterparty.
falsifiers.basis: disclosed counterparty concentration + contract amendments. PROPOSED — operator to select.

falsifiers.trigger: The frontier-to-open catch-up window WIDENS past ~6 months, removing the premise this driver INHERITS from ai-value-migration: if frontier capability does not commoditize, the scarce asset never moves down to compute at all.
falsifiers.basis: inherited premise, not this card's own claim. PROPOSED — operator to select.

They exist in this scan's own facts, and they are FOUR DIFFERENT KINDS OF NUMBER: APLD $36.2bn contracted lease revenue (1,410 MW) · CRWV $60.7bn RPO · BLZE ~$335m estimated contract value · WYFI >$160m contract value · DUOT ~$18.8m customer prepayments · CIFR $810m SENIOR SECURED NOTES ISSUED (a financing, not a customer contract) · BTBT $100m INTERCOMPANY delayed-draw loan to a WYFI subsidiary (not third-party exposure at all) · RIOT and WULF disclose NO dollar figure, only capacity (25 MW to AMD; ~1,007 MW across four leases including 401 MW to Anthropic). || SENSITIVITY OF THE PRE-REGISTERED $100m FLOOR — published because it decides whether the contamination matters. Dollar-only, as v1 was written ('no number means no binding tier'): >=$25m/$50m/$100m all keep the SAME six (APLD, BLZE, BTBT, CIFR, CRWV, WYFI); >=$160m drops BTBT to five; >=$250m drops WYFI to four; >=$500m three; >=$1bn two (APLD, CRWV). So the floor is NOT load-bearing anywhere in the $25m-$100m band, and the contamination that worried me is moot. THE TABLE SHOWS SOMETHING WORSE THAN CONTAMINATION: at EVERY floor the dollar-only gate ADMITS CIFR on a bond issuance and (below $160m) BTBT on an intercompany loan, while EXCLUDING WULF and RIOT — the two names with the largest contracted physical capacity — purely because they disclose in megawatts rather than dollars. A gate written to stop the tier selecting on FORM was itself selecting on form, in a new place: currency of disclosure. It selects close to backwards. || GATE v2, REPLACING v1 BEFORE THE NEXT RUN. (1) KIND FIRST: the magnitude must be CONTRACTED CUSTOMER ECONOMICS — contract value, RPO, contracted lease revenue, or customer prepayments/deferred revenue. A FINANCING (notes issued, credit facility, term loan) or an INTERCOMPANY transaction can never qualify a name for the binding or quantified tiers AT ANY SIZE. (2) THEN SIZE, in either unit: >=USD 100m of contracted customer economics, OR >=5 MW of contracted critical IT load where no dollar figure is disclosed. (3) Neither disclosed means neither tier, at any size. MW FLOOR BASIS: APLD discloses 1,410 MW against $36.2bn over 15-year base terms = ~$25.7m per MW, so $100m is ~3.9 MW, rounded UP to 5 MW so the floor sits on no observed value. FLAGGED AS AN INFERENCE: applying one issuer's disclosed $/MW to another issuer is a cross-name derivation, not a disclosed fact. PRE-REGISTERED EFFECT, computed before the run: APLD, BLZE, CRWV, WYFI qualify on dollars and RIOT, WULF on capacity; BTBT, CIFR and DUOT fall out. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 — an earlier version of this line claimed the crypto-origin share falls from 6-of-9 to 2-of-6. THAT WAS WRONG, and it was the only figure suggesting v2 improved the tier's COMPOSITION rather than merely its size. Under one stated entity-level rule (the operating company was founded as, or drew substantially all revenue from, crypto mining/staking before pivoting): BEFORE 6-of-9 = 67% (APLD ex-Applied Blockchain, BTBT, CIFR, CRWV founded as Atlantic Crypto, RIOT, WULF); AFTER 4-of-6 = 67% (APLD, CRWV, RIOT, WULF). THE SHARE IS UNCHANGED. Under a parent-inclusive rule that lets WYFI inherit Bit Digital's origin it goes 78% to 83% — slightly WORSE. v2 fixes the KIND defect and leaves the cohort confound exactly where it was. HONESTY ON v2's OWN PRE-REGISTRATION: it is not clean either — it was designed against the observed tier's structure. What makes it defensible is that its KIND rule is a doctrine statement derivable with no data at all (a bond raised is not a customer contract; an intercompany loan is not third-party exposure), and the SIZE floor was NOT moved from v1's $100m. || MW FLOOR SENSITIVITY (2026-09-02), run the same way as the dollar floor. Under v2, MW applies only where no dollar is disclosed — RIOT (25 MW) and WULF (~1,007 MW). >=1 MW, >=5, >=10 and >=25 all keep BOTH; >=50 keeps only WULF. So the 5 MW floor is NOT load-bearing anywhere in the 1-25 band and the concern about it dissolves. TWO CAVEATS THAT DO NOT: (i) the $25.7m/MW conversion is APLD's BLENDED figure over 15-year base terms, and applying it across issuers assumes comparable per-MW economics AND comparable duration — WULF's leases run 10-25 years and RIOT's initial term is 10, so equal MW does not mean equal contracted revenue. The conversion sets the floor's order of magnitude and nothing finer. (ii) RIOT's counterparty is AMD — a CHIP VENDOR, not an AI tenant. 25 MW leased to AMD may be silicon bring-up or internal validation rather than serving AI demand, which is a DRIVER-TIE question the magnitude gate cannot see. Flagged for adjudication: RIOT may not belong in this tier on tie grounds regardless of what any floor does. Note also RIOT sits EXACTLY on 25 MW, so a floor set there would be knife-edge; 5 MW is not near any observed value. || RELATED-PARTY SWEEP (2026-09-02) — asked whether BTBT's defect PROPAGATED. It did not: BTBT is the ONLY tier member whose grade rests on an intercompany transaction (its counterparty, Enovum NC-1 Venture LLC, is an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of White Fiber Operating Partnership, i.e. of WYFI, which BTBT ~70.5% owns and consolidates).
